[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Regularization Techniques in Machine Learning"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Overfitting is one of the most common challenges in deep learning. It occurs when a model learns the training data too well, capturing noise and outliers rather than the underlying distribution. This tutorial explores three foundational regularization techniques used to combat overfitting: Dropout, Batch Normalization, and Weight Decay."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Weight Decay (L2 Regularization)"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Weight decay adds a penalty proportional to the square of the magnitude of the weights to the loss function. This discourages the network from relying too heavily on any single feature, keeping the weights small and the decision boundaries smoother."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torch.nn as nn

# Applying Weight Decay in an Adam optimizer
model = nn.Linear(10, 2)
optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001, weight_decay=1e-4)"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Dropout"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Dropout is a stochastic regularization technique where randomly selected neurons are set to zero during training with a probability p. This prevents neurons from co-adapting and forces the network to learn redundant, robust representations."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import torch.nn as nn

class RegularizedNet(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super(RegularizedNet, self).__init__()
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(64, 32)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(p=0.5)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(32, 10)

    def forward(self, x):
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        x = self.dropout(x)
        return self.fc2(x)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Batch Normalization (BatchNorm)"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Batch Normalization normalizes the output of a previous activation layer by subtracting the batch mean and dividing by the batch standard deviation. While primarily designed to stabilize and accelerate training, it also introduces a mild regularization effect by adding noise to the training process."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"import torch.nn as nn

# Integrating BatchNorm into a sequential block
block = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(128, 64),
    nn.BatchNorm1d(64),
    nn.ReLU()
)"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary of Best Practices"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Weight Decay (L2) as a default baseline for nearly all neural network architectures."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apply Dropout primarily in dense, fully connected layers rather than convolutional layers, typically with rates between 0.2 and 0.5."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Place Batch Normalization layers after linear or convolutional operations and before activation functions."}]
